name: Rhode Island
nameStory: It is not an island, and it has nothing to do with Rhodes - probably. The name is either Dutch 'Roodt Eylandt' (red island) or an explorer's offhand comparison of Block Island to the Greek island of Rhodes. The smallest state has the least accurate name.
capitalStory: Roger Williams was banished from Massachusetts in the dead of winter for arguing that government had no business dictating religion. He named the place he landed Providence, for the divine providence he believed had saved him, and built the first colony in America with real separation of church and state.

majorFeatures.name: Narragansett Bay
majorFeatures.note: A deep bay that nearly cuts the state in half

majorFeatures.name: Atlantic Coast
majorFeatures.note: 400 miles of shoreline in a tiny state

funFacts: Rhode Island is about 1,214 square miles - you could fit 425 of them inside Alaska.
It boycotted the Constitutional Convention entirely and was the last of the thirteen to ratify, holding out until 1790.
It was also the first colony to formally renounce allegiance to the king, two months before the Declaration.
Until voters shortened it in 2020, its official name was 'State of Rhode Island and Providence Plantations' - the longest of any state.
whyItMatters: Rhode Island was founded specifically as a place where the government could not tell you what to believe. Its charter guaranteeing 'liberty in religious concernments' became a direct model for the First Amendment.
